subject: Recap + proposed architecture: SDK / Auth / Routing / Tool-calling patterns
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Sara Alvarez <sara@avacloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + proposed next steps — SDK / auth / routing / tool-calling patterns

Hi Sara (and Tom),

Great to meet earlier today — thanks for the run-through and demos. Quick recap from our side and the specific architectural questions we promised to outline so your engineers can validate timelines. TL;DR: we think a Hosted + Dedicated reserved pool in us-east is a safe first step, OIDC for auth, tool-calling via structured function definitions, and embeddings for a re-ranker on search.

Recap of needs you called out:
- Auth: prefer OIDC integration with Okta; would like short-lived runtime tokens rather than long-lived API keys.
- Throughput: baseline ~200 req/min with spikes up to ~500; many requests are short (200-400 tokens) but some batches hit ~1k tokens.
- Latency target: 250–300ms p95 for the primary flow (catalog lookup + re-rank).
- Tooling: plan to call two internal services per request in parallel (catalog lookup + pricing engine), then do an embeddings-based reranker. Need guidance on error handling and fallbacks.
- Observability / rollout: want canary rollout and rollback capability; cost-visibility is important.

Questions from our side that will shape the design:
1) Can you confirm whether AvaCloud prefers a private deployment (VPC) vs hosted with dedicated capacity?
2) For OIDC, do you need Redwood to initiate a token-exchange (on behalf of users/services), or will you provide short-lived tokens that our runtime will accept?
3) Any constraints on outbound networking from your side (e.g., some services blocked, strict IP allowlists)?
4) Preferred format for structured outputs (we recommend a JSON schema + type annotations for tool-calling).

Proposed next steps and owners:
- Rafael: schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with your infra/engineering and our engineer (Laura) — propose Mon or Tue next week.
- Laura: prepare an architecture sketch showing SDK flows, OIDC token exchange pattern, routing/fallbacks, and a tool-calling orchestration pattern.
- Monica: draft an initial mutual action plan (attached) with milestones and procurement checklist.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (SDK snippets), mutual-action-plan-avacloud.xlsx (MVP milestones)

Thanks — I’ll wait for a couple quick clarifications and propose times for the deep-dive.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Re: Recap + proposed next steps — SDK / auth / routing / tool-calling patterns

Thanks Rafael — good summary. A few clarifications from our engineering team:

- Deployment: our preference is hosted with a VPC peering/PrivateLink option if possible. We want Redwood to host but keep egress controlled. We can consider dedicated on-prem later.
- Auth: we will be using Okta and prefer an OIDC-based exchange where Redwood performs a standard OAuth 2.0 token exchange and issues short-lived runtime credentials to your runtime. We can share Okta metadata (issuer, jwks).
- Traffic: baseline 200 req/min, spikes to 500+ for flash sales windows. Sequence length: typical 300 tokens, rare up to 1k.
- Tooling: plan is to call 2–3 internal services in parallel per user query: catalog service (sync), pricing/gross-margin microservice (sync), and optionally a third async enrichment (inventory). We want the orchestration model to:
  * execute catalog + pricing in parallel,
  * fail-fast on deterministic errors from pricing (e.g., no price) and fall back to cached price,
  * continue with best-effort for async enrichment, and
  * run embedding-based reranker after receiving the tool outputs.

Error handling: we prefer explicit status envelopes back from tools (ok/warn/error) instead of relying on text parsing. If a tool times out, use cached last-known-good and surface a warning to the user. Retries should be attempted only for idempotent queries.

Can you include an example JSON schema for the structured output + tool interface? Also please propose an SLO-minded batching and caching strategy — we care about p95 latency more than token cost initially.

I attached a short doc with our non-functional requirements. Happy to jump on a technical call — Fri 11am PT works for our infra lead Tom.

Best,
Sara Alvarez
Head of Product Engineering | AvaCloud

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed next steps — SDK / auth / routing / tool-calling patterns

Sara — perfect, thanks for the detail. Short reply with concrete proposals; we’ll cover the examples during the call Tom suggested (Fri 11am PT).

High-level architecture (proposal):
- Deployment: Hosted with VPC peering to AvaCloud (private egress). Start with Redwood Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) in us-east for predictable p95. We can evaluate Dedicated -> Private later.
- Auth: OIDC token exchange pattern. Flow: AvaCloud Okta -> short-lived auth token (JWT) -> Redwood token-exchange endpoint -> Redwood runtime receives short-lived runtime token bound to request scope. SDKs will support exchanging tokens via the usual OAuth flows; sample snippet in the attached SDK quickstart.
- Routing & fallbacks: Primary routing by latency SLO to a high-capacity model. If latency or capacity constraints exceed thresholds, auto-fallback to a smaller model variant with degraded but acceptable quality.
- Tool/Function-calling pattern (recommended):
  1) Define each tool with a clear typed contract and response envelope (status, code, payload). Example: {"tool":"catalog_lookup","schema":"...","timeout_ms":200} (we’ll provide a template).
  2) Execute catalog_lookup and pricing_lookup in parallel with strict per-call timeouts (100–200ms).
  3) If pricing_lookup returns error/timeout -> fetch cached price and tag the response with warnings. If both tools fail -> fall back to a simulated best-guess or a business-rule response.
  4) After tool outputs are combined, run a small embeddings-based reranker against top-k candidates (k=5) to improve relevance. Keep the reranker model smaller to control latency.
  5) Emit structured JSON to the client matching the agreed schema; include a diagnostics block with timings, tool statuses, and model variant used for easy debugging.

Error-handling patterns we recommend:
- Use a typed status envelope from each tool: {status: 'ok'|'warn'|'error', code: string, payload: object, cached: bool}
- For transient errors, one retry only for idempotent calls. Mark non-idempotent calls as no-retry.
- Implement graceful degradation: return partial data with explicit warnings rather than failing the whole request.

Operational notes:
- Batching & caching: aggregate similar requests for the reranker in 50–150ms windows where p95 allows; use KV cache for recent catalog lookups keyed by item id + TTL.
- Observability: include per-token cost and per-route latency traces in the diagnostics block; Redwood Console dashboards can be configured for route-level SLOs.

Attached: quick architecture sketch and links to the example tool-definition Gist and a sample JSON schema. For the call Friday 11am PT, I’ll invite Laura to go through the SDK auth flow and Vivek to cover rollout/ops.

Next actions (owner):
- Laura: prepare the detailed SDK/token-exchange diagram + tool-definition template (by Thu EOD).
- Monica: update the mutual action plan with procurement and legal touchpoints.
- Sara/Tom: confirm the Fri 11am PT slot.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

-Rafael

rafael@redwood.com

Rafael / Monica — I put together the initial architecture sketch and a minimal tool-definition template (attached) you can share on the call. Key implementation notes for the engineering deep-dive: 

1) Tool definition template (minimal):
   - id: string
   - endpoint: url
   - input_schema: json-schema-url
   - output_schema: json-schema-url
   - timeout_ms: int
   - retry_policy: none|idempotent_only
   - cacheable: true|false

2) Parallel execution pattern: fan-out catalog + pricing in parallel using an async worker pool; gather results with a bounded wait (e.g., 180ms). If price missing -> hit price-cache synchronously (aim for <50ms).

3) Structured output suggestion: top-level keys: {result, tools:[], diagnostics:{timings:[], statuses:[]}, model_variant}. Sample schema attached as JSON in the gist.

4) SDK note: include helper to perform OIDC token exchange and then attach short-lived runtime token in the Authorization header. Provide example code for Node and Python.

I also annotated the arch-sketch with estimated p95 numbers and where to add metrics (per-tool latency, cache hit-rate, model token-cost).

Attached: arch-sketch.png (PNG mock), tool-definition-template.json (inline in gist)

I’ll be on the Fri 11am PT call to walk through the sequence diagrams. Rafael — can you forward the invite to Sara + Tom?
